title: Count Connected Components
statement:
A data centre has n machines, numbered 0 to n - 1. Each entry [a, b] in edges is a network cable between machines a and b. Cables work both ways. Machines that can reach each other through any chain of cables form one cluster; a machine with no cables is a cluster on its own.

Write def solution(n, edges) that returns the number of clusters as an integer.

The same pair can be cabled twice, and a cable [a, a] from a machine to itself is allowed; neither changes the answer.

examples.why: The LeetCode 323 example 2. One chain joins all five machines.
No cables: each of the 4 machines is its own cluster.

think.a: The connected components of an undirected graph with n nodes. Every node belongs to exactly one component, isolated nodes included. Start from n components: each cable that joins two different components merges them into one, so the count drops by 1.

Start with 5 clusters: {0} {1} {2} {3} {4}. Cable 0-1 merges two: 4 left. Cable 1-2 merges {0, 1} with {2}: 3 left. Cable 3-4: 2 left. Answer 2. A cable between two machines already in the same cluster would change nothing.

think.q: What is the first idea that works?
think.a: Give every machine a cluster label equal to its number. For each cable [a, b] with different labels, rewrite every machine labelled like b to a's label. Count the distinct labels at the end. Each relabel scans all n machines, so it is O(n x E).

Union-find (disjoint set union). Each cluster is a tree of parent pointers; its root names the cluster. find(x) walks up to the root, union(a, b) links one root under the other. With union by size and path halving, each operation is almost O(1). A BFS or DFS over an adjacency list also works in O(n + E); union-find shines when cables arrive one at a time.

1. parent = list(range(n)), size = [1] * n, count = n.
  2. find(x): while parent[x] != x, point x at its grandparent and move up. Return x.
  3. For each cable, find both roots. If they are equal, skip. Otherwise hang the smaller tree under the larger and subtract 1 from count.
  4. Return count.

No cables (answer n). One machine. A cable repeated, or listed both ways. A self-cable [a, a]. A cycle, whose last cable joins two machines already together. A long chain, which makes naive unions build a tall tree and makes a recursive find overflow the stack.

hints: Start with n clusters. When does one cable reduce the count, and when does it not?
Keep a parent pointer per machine; follow pointers up to a root to name the cluster. A cable joins two clusters only if their roots differ.
Make find a loop, not recursion, and shorten paths as you go (parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]). Attach the smaller tree under the bigger one.
explain:
Example 4, n = 6, edges = [[0, 1], [2, 3], [1, 3], [0, 2], [4, 4]]:

  • Start: 6 roots, count 6.
  • 0-1: roots 0 and 1 differ. Hang 1 under 0. Count 5.
  • 2-3: hang 3 under 2. Count 4.
  • 1-3: find(1) = 0, find(3) = 2. Different: hang 2 under 0. Count 3.
  • 0-2: both roots are 0. A cycle cable; skip.
  • 4-4: same root. Skip.

Return 3: {0, 1, 2, 3}, {4} and {5}. Union by size keeps every tree at most log2(n) tall, and path halving flattens it further on each find, so each cable costs almost O(1). Both choices also keep find a short loop, so no recursion is needed.
complexity: O(n + E x α(n)) time, which is effectively linear; O(n) space
